description: SSRF block list of the agent-tool sandbox, one table for both languages. Each language's guard reads the generated module (python/src/agent_tool_sandbox/_blocklist_data.py, ts/src/blocklist-data.ts). Edit this file, then run policy/gen_python.py and policy/gen-ts.mjs. Semantics: policy/README.md.

entries.rationale: 'This' network. Linux connects 0.0.0.0 to the local host.
Private-use (RFC 1918).
Carrier-grade NAT shared address space: internal to the provider's network (Tailscale uses it too). Python's ipaddress.is_private never included it.
Loopback.
Azure WireServer: a PUBLIC address the host fabric answers inside every VM (DNS, health probes, goal state, extension configuration), so no range rule catches it.
Link-local, including the cloud metadata services at 169.254.169.254 and 169.254.170.2.
Private-use (RFC 1918).
IETF protocol assignments, including the NAT64 discovery answers 192.0.0.170/31 (RFC 7050). Python exempts two anycast addresses (next two entries).
PCP anycast. IANA marks it globally reachable, so Python lets it through; it routes to the nearest PCP server, usually the local gateway. TS blocks it with the rest of the /24. DIFFERENCES.md g1.
TURN anycast; same reasoning as PCP anycast. DIFFERENCES.md g1.
Documentation (TEST-NET-1): never routed, so blocking costs nothing. DIFFERENCES.md g2.
Private-use (RFC 1918).
Benchmarking; not globally reachable.
Documentation (TEST-NET-2). DIFFERENCES.md g2.
Documentation (TEST-NET-3). DIFFERENCES.md g2.
Multicast.
Reserved for future use, including the limited broadcast 255.255.255.255.
Unspecified ::, loopback ::1 and the deprecated IPv4-compatible addresses ::a.b.c.d. Python also blocks it through v6-reserved-0000.

IPv4-mapped, blocked whole: a resolver never needs to answer a mapped address for a public host, and a mapped literal in a URL is only an evasion spelling. When on, it overrides v6-ipv4-mapped-decode. TS blocks the whole /96; Python decodes instead. DIFFERENCES.md g3.

IPv4-mapped, judged by the embedded IPv4 alone (low 32 bits) when v6-ipv4-mapped is off. In Python the guard unwraps mapped DNS answers to IPv4 before the check (_resolve_host_ips; pinning._checked_addresses), so through the guard the embedded address meets the whole IPv4 table. decode_excludes only matters for a mapped IPv6Address handed straight to _ip_is_blocked: the ipaddress.is_* properties this table replaced delegate to the embedded IPv4 (CPython 3.13+, and the 2024 backports to 3.10-3.12), but the CGNAT and WireServer checks were IPv4Address-only, so a raw ::ffff:100.64.0.1 was allowed. Kept for zero behaviour change (tests/test_parity_in_tree.py IP corpus); unreachable through the guard.
IPv4-translated (SIIT): ::ffff:0:a.b.c.d reaches the embedded IPv4 through a translator. Python also blocks it through v6-reserved-0000.

NAT64 well-known prefix, blocked whole: a translator turns it into IPv4 connections. Costs IPv6-only DNS64 hosts every IPv4-only site (see DIFFERENCES.md, 'DNS64 / NAT64 compatibility trade-offs'). When on, it overrides v6-nat64-wkp-decode. Python blocks it whole (it sits in v6-reserved-0000); TS decodes. DIFFERENCES.md g4.

NAT64 well-known prefix, judged by the embedded IPv4 alone (the last 32 bits, RFC 6052 §2.1) when v6-nat64-wkp is off: DNS64 answers for public IPv4-only hosts stay reachable, private embeddings are blocked. The decode inherits the IPv4 table, gaps included (emb-nat64-test-net).
Local-use NAT64 prefix, blocked whole: not globally reachable, and the operator picks the embedding length, so the IPv4 cannot be located reliably.

IANA reserved (IPv4-compatible, mapped and translated space, NAT64 prefixes). Also covers what TS lets through: 64:ff9b::/32 outside the /96 and /48 (g5) and the odd ::/8 shapes ::1:ffff:0:0, ::ffff:0:0:7f00:1, ::1:7f00:1 (g12).
IANA reserved (holds the discard-only 100::/64). DIFFERENCES.md g10.
Discard-only prefix (remote-triggered black hole); not globally reachable. Inside v6-reserved-0100. DIFFERENCES.md g10.
IANA reserved (formerly OSI NSAP). DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.

IETF protocol assignments (benchmarking 2001:2::/48, deprecated ORCHID 2001:10::/28, SRP anycast 2001:1::3, ...), minus the IANA globally-reachable exemptions below. TS blocks only Teredo inside it. DIFFERENCES.md g8.
Teredo, blocked whole: the client IPv4 is obfuscated and the server IPv4 is whatever the attacker picks, so no embedded check holds. Python also blocks it through v6-ietf-2001-23.
PCP anycast, IANA globally reachable. Allowed by both languages (TS blocks the IPv4 twin 192.0.0.9, see DIFFERENCES.md 'Both languages allow').
TURN anycast, IANA globally reachable. Allowed by both languages.
AMT (automatic multicast tunneling), IANA globally reachable.
AS112-v6 (DNAME redirection sink), IANA globally reachable.
ORCHIDv2, IANA globally reachable.
Drone remote ID protocol entity tags (DETs), IANA globally reachable.
Documentation: never routed. DIFFERENCES.md g9.
6to4, blocked whole (public embeddings too): a host or relay with 6to4 tunnels to the IPv4 in bits 16-47; no agent tool needs 6to4, and decoding would inherit the IPv4 table.
Documentation: never routed. DIFFERENCES.md g9.
IANA reserved (includes the SRv6 SID block 5f00::/16, RFC 9602). DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
Unique local addresses (the IPv6 RFC 1918), including AWS IMDS fd00:ec2::254.
IANA reserved. DIFFERENCES.md g12.
Link-local (zone IDs are ignored for the match).
Site-local, deprecated but still routed inside some networks.
Multicast.

entries.name: localhost
entries.rationale: Refused by name before DNS (trailing dots ignored): stub resolvers answer it without asking DNS, and a lying resolver or /etc/hosts could answer anything.
Every name under .localhost is loopback; refused by name before DNS (trailing dots ignored).
